contrast: *Undocumented* is the neutral term in American news writing for a person without legal papers; *illegal immigrant* is dated and many people find it offensive, and *an illegal* as a noun more so.

senses.gloss: Living or working in a country without the legal papers that allow it.

senses.gloss: Not written down, recorded or backed by evidence.
examples: The app has a few *undocumented* features.
His claims about the money are completely *undocumented*.

position: predicative only — after a verb: *leave it undone*, *came undone*

senses.gloss: Not finished; not taken care of.

senses.gloss: No longer tied or buttoned.

senses.gloss: With your clothes off.

position: attributive only — before a noun: *undue delay*, *undue influence*

senses.gloss: More than is necessary or reasonable.

senses.gloss: Not deserved.

senses.gloss: Worried; not comfortable about something.

senses.gloss: Not settled or secure; likely to break down.

senses.gloss: Not showing feelings; calm and matter-of-fact.

She stayed *unemotional* through the whole hearing.

senses.gloss: Not able to get a job, because of a lack of skills, poor health or a record.

position: both — before a noun, or after a verb with *by*

senses.gloss: Not good for your plans; working against you.

position: both — before a noun, or after a verb with *by*

senses.gloss: Not completed.

senses.gloss: Of wood or furniture: not painted, stained or varnished.

senses.gloss: Not in good physical condition.

senses.gloss: Showing someone in a bad light; not complimentary.

senses.gloss: Not turning away from something hard or ugly; steady and brave.

senses.gloss: Without a clear aim; not concentrating.

senses.gloss: Blurry; not sharp.

senses.gloss: Not expected or predicted.

senses.gloss: Harsh; leaving no room for mistakes.

senses.gloss: Not willing to forgive people.

senses.gloss: Unlucky or badly chosen — of an event or a decision.

The house had been *uninhabited* for years.
Most of the region is *uninhabited*.

senses.gloss: Free and open in the way you behave; not shy or held back.
examples: She is an *uninhibited* dancer.
Two drinks in, he gets loud and *uninhibited*.
The show is famous for its *uninhibited* humor.

contrast: *Uninspired* describes work with no spark in it; *uninspiring* describes a thing that gives you no spark: *an uninspired performance* by a tired band, *an uninspiring menu* that leaves you cold.

senses.gloss: Dull and ordinary; showing no spark.
examples: The cooking was competent but *uninspired*.
It was an *uninspired* performance.
The new logo looks *uninspired*.

senses.gloss: Not exciting or encouraging anyone.
examples: It was an *uninspiring* start to the season.
The choices on the ballot are *uninspiring*.
He gave a flat, *uninspiring* talk.

senses.gloss: Of a person: having no health or car insurance.
examples: Millions of Americans are still *uninsured*.
An *uninsured* driver hit her car.

senses.gloss: Of property or a loss: not covered by insurance.
examples: The flood damage was *uninsured*.
They face thousands of dollars in *uninsured* losses.

senses.gloss: Impossible to understand or to make out.
examples: The recording is *unintelligible* in places.
His speech was slurred and *unintelligible*.
The form is *unintelligible* to anyone but a lawyer.

senses.gloss: Not planned or not meant to happen.
examples: The law had *unintended* consequences.
There was an *unintended* pause that got the biggest laugh.
Any resemblance to real people is *unintended*.

contrast: The adverb *unintentionally* is the common form: *I unintentionally left her off the list*.

senses.gloss: Not done on purpose.
examples: The insult was *unintentional*, but it still stung.
It was an *unintentional* slip.
Any errors in the list are *unintentional*.

contrast: *Uninteresting* is the thing; *uninterested* is the person (*He was uninterested in the offer*). *Disinterested* is a third word: it means 'having nothing to gain' — a *disinterested* judge, not a bored one.

senses.gloss: Not holding your attention; dull.
examples: The first half of the book is *uninteresting*.
He found the whole subject *uninteresting*.
It is a technically *uninteresting* problem.

position: both — before a noun, or after a verb: *She worked uninterrupted*

senses.gloss: Going on without a break, or not blocked by anything.
examples: I need two *uninterrupted* hours to finish this.
The room has an *uninterrupted* view of the bay.
He slept *uninterrupted* for ten hours.

position: both — before a noun, or after a verb: *showed up uninvited*

senses.gloss: Coming or given without being asked for.
examples: An *uninvited* guest showed up with a six-pack.
He walked in *uninvited*.
She is tired of *uninvited* advice about her kids.

contrast: American English writes *unionize*, *unionized* with a *z*; the *-ise* spelling is British.

senses.gloss: Belonging to a labor union — of workers or of a workplace.
examples: The plant is fully *unionized*.
*Unionized* workers earn about 15 percent more on average.
Only one of their stores is *unionized*.

senses.gloss: Made for both men and women.
examples: The gym has a *unisex* locker room.
It is a *unisex* fragrance.
The shirts come in *unisex* sizes only.

takes: *in* + noun or *-ing*, in sense 2 (*united in grief*)
contrast: Capitalized in names: *the United States*, *the United Nations*, *the United Kingdom*.

senses.gloss: Joined together into one country, group or organization.
examples: A *united* Germany came in 1990.
They campaigned for a *united* Ireland.

senses.gloss: In agreement; acting together.
examples: The family is *united* in its grief.
The party is *more united* than it was a year ago.

contrast: *Unjust* is formal and belongs to laws, rulings and systems; for everyday complaints say *unfair*: *It is unfair that she got a bigger piece*.

senses.gloss: Not fair or right — especially of a law, a system or a punishment.
examples: They call the sentence *unjust*.
He spent his life fighting an *unjust* system.
Nothing is *more unjust* than punishing the wrong person.

senses.gloss: Impossible to defend with any good reason.
examples: The delay is *unjustifiable*.
He called the spending *unjustifiable*.
It was an *unjustifiable* use of force.

contrast: *Unjustified* says there was no good reason for it this time; *unjustifiable* says there could never be one.

senses.gloss: Not supported by a good reason; not deserved.
examples: The fear turned out to be *unjustified*.
She complained about *unjustified* charges on the bill.
His confidence was entirely *unjustified*.
